gap: No result ChatGPT got states that UGREEN's own store sells two models under the DXP2800 name: the Intel N100 DXP2800 at $389.99 and the AMD Ryzen Embedded R2514 DXP2800 GT at $429.99. UGREEN's Jellyfin guide says the GT models 'use AMD processors and therefore have no Intel Quick Sync path' and need VA-API, so the 'select Intel QSV' setup ChatGPT gave does not work on the GT.
standout_why: Pages compared: Starry Hope best-2-bay (cited in two chats), ComputingForGeeks QuickSync picks, Jellyfin's Intel hardware-acceleration doc and its GitHub copy (cited), and UGREEN's own Jellyfin install blog (in results but not cited). Starry Hope lists the DXP2800 GT with 'Yes, H.264 and H.265' transcoding but never says it has no Quick Sync or needs VA-API. ComputingForGeeks does not mention the GT at all. Every ChatGPT answer tells the shopper to pick Intel QSV and never warns about the GT. Starry Hope already states the DH2300 has no official Docker support and that DS225+ hardware transcoding fails on stock DSM, so those findings are not new.
decides: It confirms the DXP2800 pick and tightens it. Buy the plain N100 DXP2800 ($389.99 at UGREEN on 2026-11-13), not the GT. The GT is over the $400 budget and needs VA-API, not QSV. Separately, our page's DH2300 row ('Manual Docker only; direct play') contradicts UGREEN, which says the DH2300 'cannot host Jellyfin because it lacks Docker support'; that row should say it cannot run Jellyfin. The F2-425 Plus is $469.99 at TerraMaster's store today, so it falls outside this question's budget unless a retailer has it lower.

findings.label: Jellyfin acceleration path
findings.value: No Intel Quick Sync. Use VA-API with /dev/dri/renderD128 (Playback > Transcoding > Video Acceleration API)
findings.source_title: How to Install Jellyfin on UGREEN NAS: App Center or Docker
findings.note: UGREEN blog dated 2025-12-11, quoted: DXP2800 GT and DXP4800 GT 'use AMD processors and therefore have no Intel Quick Sync path'.

findings.label: UGREEN US store price
findings.note: From storecheck.py search of ai.ugreen.com for 'DXP2800'. Over the $400 budget.

findings.note: From storecheck.py search on the same day. The same search returned the DXP2800 + Docking Station bundle at $424.99 and the refurbished DXP2800 at $269.99, which is unavailable.

findings.label: Jellyfin on Intel DXP models
findings.value: App Center package or Docker. Hardware Acceleration set to Intel QuickSync (QSV), device /dev/dri/renderD128. Docker also needs group_add with the NAS's render/video group IDs
findings.source_title: How to Install Jellyfin on UGREEN NAS: App Center or Docker
findings.note: UGREEN's support table covers 'Intel DXP models' but does not name each model. The page's own Compose example maps /dev/dri:/dev/dri, while its Intel section maps /dev/dri/renderD128. To check it works, the FFmpeg log should show 'qsv'.

findings.label: Jellyfin support (maker-stated exclusion)
findings.value: Cannot host Jellyfin; no Docker support
findings.source_title: How to Install Jellyfin on UGREEN NAS: App Center or Docker
findings.note: UGREEN quote: the DH2300 'cannot host Jellyfin because it lacks Docker support'. This contradicts our current row ('Manual Docker only; direct play'). The DH4300 Plus (also ARM) is supported through the App Center with Rockchip MPP (RKMPP).

findings.label: Jellyfin Intel encoder limits
findings.value: Gen 11 JSL/EHL graphics only support LP (low-power) encoding mode. ICL/JSL/EHL and older are 'losing support for QSV on Linux'. No AV1 decode on Jasper Lake; AV1 decode needs Gen 12 (Tiger Lake) or newer
findings.note: Applies to N5095 models such as the TerraMaster F2-425/F2-423/F4-423 and the N4505 QNAP TS-262. LP encoding relies on HuC firmware on the host. The doc also says the official Docker image ships the Intel media drivers and OpenCL runtime.
